ankit (customer): hey @support, we're seeing a ton of vector-db rejects after calling /v1/embeddings. Looks like dims are sometimes 512 but we expect 1536. Also billing spiked. Repro + payload below, pls help.
ankit (customer): curl we used:
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"text-embed-large-1536","input":[["Why does my embed have wrong dims?"]]}'
```
support-bot: Received customer report, creating ticket #SUP-1729 and attaching request logs. :white_check_mark:
samira (support): thanks @ankit — quick Qs: 1) can you paste the raw response you got from the embeddings API? 2) what client / SDK version? 3) do you call the embed output directly into your vector DB or transform it?
ankit (customer): response body (redacted):
```
{"data":[{"embedding":[0.001,0.0002,...],"index":0}],"model":"text-embed-small-512","usage":{"input_tokens":12}}
```
ankit (customer): we were expecting model text-embed-large-1536. Our code sets model param but we recently upgraded an internal helper — could be a bug.
samira (support): hm that explains the dim mismatch — the API returned a 512-dim vector from model "text-embed-small-512". Two likely causes: either the request payload specified the smaller model, or our routing/fallback swapped to the smaller model due to capacity/cost policy. Can you confirm the exact JSON you sent? you pasted earlier with nested array around input — I suspect nested-array vs scalar ambiguity might trigger different code path in your SDK.
ankit (customer): yes the payload we POSTed is same as earlier (note the double brackets around input). we thought passing `input: [ [ "str" ] ]` would be fine for single-batch item (we wrap per-customer batches). but maybe that changed.
carlos (eng-runtime): looking at logs from infra (correlating request id from ticket) — server received model="text-embed-large-1536" in top-level metadata, but the parsed body had input as an array containing a single array. Our request router includes a small heuristic: if the input items are all arrays of numbers/bytes/length < 20 tokens we sometimes route to the small model to optimize cost (it assumes customers passed pre-tokenized numeric arrays). In this case the nested array pattern confused the heuristic and we routed to text-embed-small-512. I'll paste the snippet from the router logs:
```
[router] req=abcd1234 model_hint=text-embed-large-1536 body.input=[["Why does my embed have wrong dims?"]]
[router] heuristic: payload looks like pre-tokenized arrays -> route candidate=text-embed-small-512
[router] selected=text-embed-small-512
```
samira (support): ohhh. so nested arrays triggered the heuristic. that explains the billing spike too (we billed per-embedding call to small model but customer processed as if they had large model vectors and re-inserted into DB causing rejects). We should surface a clearer validation error instead of silent routing.
ankit (customer): thanks — can you recommend a fix now? is there a quick workaround while you patch the router?
carlos (eng-runtime): immediate workaround: send input as either a flat string (single item) or a flat array of strings for batches. Example correct payloads:
```
# single input (string)
{"model":"text-embed-large-1536","input":"Why does my embed have wrong dims?"}

# batch of two inputs (array of strings)
{"model":"text-embed-large-1536","input":["first text","second text"]}
```
carlos (eng-runtime): and avoid passing nested arrays like `[ ["..." ] ]`. If you must keep the wrapper in your app, ensure you call JSON.stringify on the inner item and pass the inner string directly in the request body.
ankit (customer): ok that fixed it locally — toggled my helper to collapse single-item batches and now API returns model text-embed-large-1536 with 1536 floats. thanks.
samira (support): we'll keep this ticket open until eng pushes a change. Carlos, proposal: 1) add strict validation at API ingress that rejects input shapes we consider ambiguous with a 400 + clear message; 2) log an informational note when routing falls back to smaller model due to heuristic; 3) short-term add a note in docs/faq about nested arrays.
carlos (eng-runtime): agreed. I'll create ENG-449 to add explicit shape validation + clearer error text: "input must be string or array of strings; nested arrays may be interpreted as pre-tokenized inputs and route to a different model". Will also add a quick sniff to prefer explicit model param over heuristic routing.
samira (support): elevation planned. For now I've added a snippet to the ticket with the correct/incorrect payload examples and a recommended client hotfix. Also adding a KB entry: "Embeddings: nested arrays can trigger heuristic routing to smaller model -> wrong dims" and linking to PR once Carlos opens it. :memo:
dev-bot: Ticket SUP-1729 updated: status=escalated assignee=carlos priority=high
ankit (customer): appreciate it — one more q: will I be refunded for extra calls that hit the wrong model? we had ~3k calls with small model before noticing.
samira (support): i'll review usage and escalate billing request to finance after eng confirms behavior window. For immediate relief, i'll issue temporary credit while we investigate — 24–48h SLA for billing review.
carlos (eng-runtime): will follow up in ENG-449 with timeline. thanks for the clear repro, @ankit. that helped us pinpoint the router heuristic quickly. :zap:
ankit (customer): thanks everyone — the team is unblocked. will keep ticket open until you close.
